newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debts slip in cautious trade before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debts slip in cautious trade before FOMC.

text.p: Prices of emerging market debts were mostly lower in lackluster trading on Monday ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

"The whole sentiment could change after the FOMC meeting," said a trader. The FOMC meets Tuesday and Wednesday to deliberate on credit policy. The majority of market analysts expect no change in U.S. interest rates.
Russia eked out small gains, but the advance fell short of what traders had hoped in the wake of the budget progress and the funds released by the International Monetary Fund.
After rising in early European trading, "there was no followthrough," a trader said.
Russia's dollar Vnesh edged up 1/4 to 77 bid, Min Fin 3 was unchanged at 83-1/2 bid.
Over the weekend, the Russian parliament passed the first reading of the state budget and the IMF released the October tranche of the $10.2 billion loan.
Gary Evans, strategist at Lehman Brothers, said continuing concerns about Russia's political risk are holding investors back.
"Russia is a going to be a major economic superpower, after it gets through this transition," he said.
Brazil reported a $853 million trade deficit for November in line with expectations.
